title: The remedy for an unset or relative HOMEBREW_PREFIX is to install devbin with Homebrew, which loops when devbin is installed
body:
When HOMEBREW_PREFIX is unset or not absolute, `devbin_brew_root` finds no Homebrew install, by design: a process started without the login profile (cron, a hook a GUI app launched, a bare ssh command), or a profile that puts Homebrew's bin on PATH without `brew shellenv`, has no HOMEBREW_PREFIX. A bare `devbin use` with no link, the note devbin writes when it vendors into a project and the machine names no install, and fleet's sweep then say why in `brew_unplaced_why`'s words ("HOMEBREW_PREFIX is not set"), and give the remedy for a formula that is not installed: "install devbin with Homebrew". With devbin installed, following it changes nothing, and the next run says the same. `use brew`'s refusal has given the remedy for each cause together since 0235 ("install devbin with Homebrew, with HOMEBREW_PREFIX exported as brew shellenv exports it"), and each site writes its remedy out for itself. Raised by cc's critic-shell review of 0235; the report's and the note's wording shipped before it.

## Cause

Measured on main at 15f2a973.

- `lib/helpers:3677-3686`: `devbin_brew_root` answers only for an absolute HOMEBREW_PREFIX. `lib/helpers:3693-3700`: `brew_unplaced_why` says which cause it is: unset, not absolute, or no devbin under an absolute prefix.
- `lib/cmd/use:63-70`: `_use_report`'s branch for no link, when `devbin_brew_root` finds nothing, prints `_use_brew_none`'s sentence and then "install devbin with Homebrew, or run <invoke> use dev or opt in the devbin checkout" (:68), and returns 1. `<invoke>` is DEVBIN_INVOKE, the running launcher. `_use_in_checkout` (:108-113) refuses `use dev` and `use opt` from any launcher but the dev checkout's own, so from an opt install or a keg this line names a command that is refused. dc's critic-shell review of 0252 found it, and vc measured it on 2026-10-27: run from the brew keg with HOMEBREW_PREFIX unset, a bare `use` printed "run /opt/homebrew/Cellar/devbin/0.1.15/libexec/bin/devbin use dev or opt in the devbin checkout". The sentences below that say `devbin use` share the flaw whenever the devbin on PATH is an opt install or a keg.
- `lib/install:110`: `source_token_note`, which `manifest_write` calls for every tree but an install (:1192), warns "this machine names no devbin install (<brew_unplaced_why's clause>), so this project's next upgrade will ask for --from until one is named: install devbin with Homebrew, or run devbin use dev or opt in the devbin checkout". No arm holds this sentence.
- `bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:610`: `sweep_source` refuses with "install devbin with Homebrew, or run devbin use opt in the devbin checkout" when `machine_install_root` names nothing; fleet.bats:1968 holds that wording.
- `lib/cmd/use:122-125`: `_use_no_brew`'s `absent` remedy names the export; use.bats:144 holds it.
- `lib/cmd/vendor:129` and `lib/cmd/upgrade:190`: with no install named, each refuses with "<source_unplaced_why> -- name one with --from <dir>", which names neither the Homebrew directory nor the export. dc's from-brew walk of 0.1.15 (2026-10-27, ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-dc/walk015/run-20261027-0916Z/, steps 101 and 102) ran each in a project with no HOMEBREW_PREFIX and read "HOMEBREW_PREFIX is not set -- name one with --from <dir>".
- `lib/cmd/doctor:969`: the switch check passes "switch: no link, so brew" whenever there is no link, without asking whether Homebrew has a devbin. So in the walk's step 100, with no HOMEBREW_PREFIX, doctor printed "ok switch: no link, so brew" while its source row in the same run said that this machine names no devbin install.
- The walk's step 105: `install --into` from the brew keg, with no HOMEBREW_PREFIX, printed the vendoring note's "or run devbin use dev or opt in the devbin checkout" to a brew user.
- `lib/cmd/shell-init:179` also says "install devbin with Homebrew", for another cause: a `dvb` emitted with no install prefix, where installing and emitting `dvb` from that install is the remedy. It is outside this issue.
- installhints.bats (:47) reads a hint as Homebrew's when it says `brew install <tool>`, and then asks for a Linux route on the same line. None of these remedies says that, and the fix keeps it so.

## Fix

One remedy, beside `brew_unplaced_why` and keyed by the same cause: for an unset or relative HOMEBREW_PREFIX, export it as `brew shellenv` exports it, in the profile the process reads; for no devbin under an absolute prefix, install devbin with Homebrew. Each site above, `use brew`'s refusal, vendor's and upgrade's refusals and doctor's switch check included, says that remedy in place of its own, so the remedy and the cause it answers cannot part. The wording holds as written on Linux and on macOS, where Homebrew's prefix differs.

dev and opt are the maintainer's alone (hv's directive 15: they are named only where a doc speaks to the maintainer of a dev checkout, never as the way a user installs). So the remedy adds "or run bin/devbin use dev or opt in your devbin checkout" only when the devbin running is a dev or opt tree, which is the maintainer's. It names the checkout's own `bin/devbin`, as `_use_in_checkout`'s refusal does (lib/cmd/use:112), because no other launcher runs `use dev` or `use opt`: not the running install's own, and not the devbin on PATH when that is an opt install or a keg. From a brew keg, the reader may be any user, so the remedy is the Homebrew one alone. That covers a bare `devbin use` run from the keg, and the vendoring note an `install --into` from the keg prints. This is vc's reading of the directive, for cc's question of 2026-10-27.

## Done when

1. With HOMEBREW_PREFIX unset, and again with it relative, a bare `devbin use` with no link, vendoring's note, fleet's sweep and `use brew`'s refusal each give exporting HOMEBREW_PREFIX as the remedy, and none tells the user to install devbin. An arm for each, red on main, and green at the fix.
2. With HOMEBREW_PREFIX absolute and no devbin under it, each still gives installing devbin with Homebrew as the remedy.
3. Each site takes its remedy from the one place beside `brew_unplaced_why`, and none spells its own.
4. With HOMEBREW_PREFIX unset, vendor and upgrade refuse giving the shared remedy beside --from. doctor's switch check does not pass "no link, so brew": it notes that no Homebrew devbin was found, says why in `brew_unplaced_why`'s words, and gives the remedy. An arm for each, red on main, and green at the fix.
5. Run from a brew keg, no remedy names dev or opt. Run from a dev or opt tree, the remedy may add `bin/devbin use dev` or `opt` in the devbin checkout, and it names no other launcher for them. An arm for each, at the vendoring note and at a bare `devbin use`, the opt tree's arm among them.
6. use.bats, fleet.bats, machinepointer.bats, doctor.bats, the files holding vendor's and upgrade's arms and the file holding vendoring's note's arm pass at the fix under BSD and GNU, beside the tree scans (installhints.bats among them) and help.
7. CI's run on the pushed head is green on Test on Ubuntu.

## Deferred to 0.1.17

hv deferred this to devbin 0.1.17 on 2026-10-28 ("defer E to 0.1.17, close 0274 and 0278", relayed verbatim by molt-vc at 18:11Z by date -u). It was built in cc's stage 8 bank for 0.1.16 (s8-rebuild adc44833 in ~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/s8/s8a/build, on dc's e3c9c8bb), which had not finished its checks or run. It is not started for 0.1.17: the bank is kept as a starting point and is rebuilt on 0.1.17's base, then checked, run and reviewed as new.

## Resolution

- The remedy for no Homebrew devbin is keyed by its cause and said once, beside brew_unplaced_why (brew_unplaced_fix): export HOMEBREW_PREFIX as brew shellenv does when it is unset or relative, install devbin with Homebrew under an absolute prefix holding none, and use dev or opt only from a dev or opt tree, by the checkout's bin/devbin (directive 15). use, doctor's switch row, vendor, upgrade, install, fleet's sweep and a link that leads nowhere all give it.
- The use.bats arm for a link that leads nowhere holds nothing after the remedy from a keg by a line ending with it, which holds when that line is the last.
- Landed on main: `5c7e6819`, `6a0d32d2` (the second is the fix for hv's run 20261029-1314).
- Arms: use.bats, a bare use's remedy by cause and from each tree; every remedy is brew_unplaced_fix's; use brew with no Homebrew devbin; a link that leads nowhere; doctor.bats, the switch row with no link and no Homebrew devbin, with and without DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX; machinepointer.bats, vendor, upgrade and their notes; fleet.bats, the sweep's refusal.
- Desk evidence: hv's full run 20261029-1314, 2826 counted, ran every arm above ok but use.bats's link-that-leads-nowhere arm, whose newline-suffix assertion could not hold on a last line. Run 20261029-1336 (`--failed`) ran it ok at the fix, 2 of 2 ok, so main at 5085ae24 is green.
